types: The one-mark items that open the AS papers. Every one here has its answer.
Explain and suggest questions (3 and 4 marks)
Point-marked questions: two developed points, or one point and its explanation. No levels and no evaluation.
Short questions on a figure in the Resource Booklet or the paper: describe, compare or suggest a reason, using the data.
Levels-marked questions that ask you to explain or analyse, worth 6 (AS and A level) or 8 marks (A level). The top level needs accurate, linked explanation; there is no evaluation mark.

The Assess and Evaluate questions: 12-mark Assess at AS and A level, 16-mark AS synoptic Evaluate, 20-mark A-level Evaluate and the 18- and 24-mark Paper 3 questions. The top level needs a sustained argument and a substantiated conclusion.
AS Paper 1 Q3/Q6 and Paper 2 Q3/Q6: questions on fieldwork in a glaciated, coastal, regenerating or diverse place, from sampling and methods to the reliability of the conclusions.
Every question where the marks need a calculation or a statistical test: means, standard deviation, Spearman's rank, chi-squared, percentages and rates of change.
Questions the mark scheme calls synoptic, every Paper 3 question and the AS 16-mark Evaluate questions, which draw on more than one topic.
searchHint: e.g. hazard risk equation, sediment cell, TNCs, superpowers
levelsNote: Pearson marks the 6- and 8-mark questions in three levels and the 12-, 16-, 18-, 20- and 24-mark questions in four. The top level needs accurate knowledge applied throughout, a balanced argument that uses evidence, and a conclusion that follows from it.

pastPapersNote: Every paper is from Pearson's own site. There were no exams in June 2020 or June 2021; the October 2020 papers are the papers printed for the cancelled summer 2020 exams, and the November 2021 series had no AS papers. The June 2022 AS papers were shorter than usual. The June 2026 papers will be added when Pearson releases them, expected after the summer 2027 exams.
latestNote: Pearson keeps each summer's papers secure for about a year: the June 2026 papers are expected after the summer 2027 exams.
